abstract: Sterile alpha motif and histidine-aspartic acid domain-containing protein 1 (SAMHD1) is a deoxynucleoside triphosphate triphosphohydrolase (dNTPase) involved in intracellular nucleotide homeostasis, antiviral restriction, and genome maintenance. While human SAMHD1 (hSAMHD1) contributes to DNA replication fork stability and DNA double-strand break repair, the corresponding functions of murine SAMHD1 (mSAMHD1) remain poorly characterized. Here, we generated SAMHD1-deficient murine GL261 glioma cells using CRISPR/Cas9 to investigate mSAMHD1 function in DNA replication. SAMHD1 knockout increased intracellular dATP levels, altered replication fork dynamics, and reduced camptothecin (CPT)-induced nascent DNA degradation, supporting conserved replication-associated functions. RNA sequencing detected transcripts corresponding to all three annotated mSamhd1 isoforms, with isoform 1 predominating, followed by isoforms 2 and 3. To assess isoform-specific functions, individual murine isoforms were expressed in SAMHD1-deficient human HEK293T cells, enabling direct comparison in a SAMHD1-null background. Both major murine isoforms, mSAMHD1 isoforms 1 and 2, localized to the nucleus, exhibited nucleotide-dependent oligomerization and retained dNTPase activity. Notably, both isoforms restored replication fork dynamics and camptothecin (CPT)-induced nascent DNA degradation to levels largely comparable to hSAMHD1. In contrast, isoform 3 exhibited markedly reduced ectopic expression, consistent with its low endogenous transcript abundance in primary murine cells, limiting functional characterization. Together, these findings demonstrate that the two major murine SAMHD1 isoforms retain replication-associated functions of hSAMHD1 despite differences in their C-terminal regions. Furthermore, the established SAMHD1-deficient GL261 cells provide a model for future studies of SAMHD1 function in glioma and its tumor immune microenvironment.
